abstract: <jats:p>This study develops an interpretable machine-learning framework with uncertainty quantification for regional ecological risk prediction. The dataset is organized as a county-month panel containing 2,400 observations and 48 predictors from land-use, landscape-pattern, climate, topographic, hydrological, and human-disturbance variables. The ecological risk target is constructed as a three-class label, including low, medium, and high risk, based on a composite ecological risk index. Python 3.11 is used for data cleaning, median imputation, z-score standardization, XGBoost classification, SHAP interpretation, and Bayesian bootstrap interval estimation. The XGBoost model is trained with fixed hyperparameters, while SHAP TreeExplainer produces global and local feature-attribution outputs. Bayesian bootstrap analysis was conducted for 500 iterations for calculating 95% confidence intervals for class probabilities and SHAP importance for features. The findings reveal that the accuracy of the model is 0.872 ± 0.021, the macro F1 score is 0.856 ± 0.026, and the macro AUC score is 0.931 ± 0.018. The average value of the 95% probability intervals width is 0.118 ± 0.027. Among others, the proportion of built-up areas, roads, patches, NDVI, rainfall, and run-off index have the highest SHAP</jats:p>
title: Research on Interpretable Machine Learning with Uncertainty Quantification for Ecological Risk Prediction
